name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPR-55U 'Undercut'
description:
The KPR-55U is Kang-Petrov's attempt to address a specific complaint from GLMZ's shelf district operators: that the KPR-74C's standard handguard makes it difficult to mount a suppressor without burning your hand on the gas tube. The KPR-55U is a 5.56mm Combat Standard variant with a redesigned receiver and handguard — the handguard is free-floated, meaning it does not contact the barrel, and features four sets of Kang-Petrov's proprietary accessory slots that are compatible with approximately 60% of the aftermarket accessories designed for Tessera's SDC-1 rail system, which Kang-Petrov has documented nowhere in any official capacity and which everyone in GLMZ knows about. The gas block has been lowered to sit below the handguard profile, eliminating the heat bleed that made suppressor use uncomfortable on earlier KP rifles. The barrel is 410mm, nearly identical to the KPR-74C, and the gas system retains the two-position adjustable regulator. The overall aesthetic is slightly more deliberate than the standard KPR — the undercut receiver corners, the continuous accessory rail, the low-profile gas block — but it is still stamped steel and polymer, and it still looks like a Kang-Petrov rifle if you have been looking at Kang-Petrov rifles long enough.

The KPR-55U is a suppressor-owner's rifle, and the suppressor market in GLMZ is a Tier 2-3 phenomenon. Tier 1 operators typically cannot afford quality suppression and do not operate in environments where the noise signature is a primary concern. Tier 2-3 operators — fixers, contractors, people who work in the proximity of infrastructure they do not want to damage acoustically — buy the KPR-55U as a platform and then spend as much again on a suppressor and optic. The Tessera rail compatibility is a quiet acknowledgment that Tier 2 buyers aspire to Tessera accessories even when they are buying Kang-Petrov rifles.

The KPR-55U develops an interesting wear pattern at the accessory slots — the slot edges accumulate a fine burr from accessories being mounted and dismounted repeatedly, and experienced users deburr them with a file on a maintenance schedule that reveals how often they are reconfiguring. A KPR-55U with smooth, rounded slot edges has been configured the same way for a long time. One with sharp, fresh burrs is being adapted to something new. Fixers who work the Wicker-Pilsen transition zone read this the way a mechanic reads engine wear — it tells you something about the operator's history without them saying a word.
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm Combat Standard
effective_range: 380m
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic / Full-automatic
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.5 kg
tactical_use: The KPR-55U is run by operators who prioritize acoustic and flash signature reduction. The free-floated barrel and suppressor-compatible design allow the rifle to be run suppressed without the thermal and accuracy issues that plagued earlier KP platforms. Operators typically pair it with a quality suppressor and a low-magnification variable optic on the accessory rail — the Tessera compatibility opens up the secondary market for used Tessera components that filters down from Tier 3-4 operators upgrading their own gear. In GLMZ's dense urban environments, a suppressed KPR-55U reduces the acoustic signature enough to complicate source triangulation by Arcturus Civil Security's audio monitoring systems.
cultural_context: The KPR-55U's secret Tessera rail compatibility is the kind of thing that gets discussed in hushed, slightly conspiratorial tones in GLMZ's fixer community. The official story is that the measurements are coincidental. The unofficial story is that a Kang-Petrov engineer who previously worked at Tessera made a specific set of design decisions that Slagworks Industrial's legal team has never formally acknowledged. Whether true or not, the practical effect is a rifle that lets Tier 2 operators access Tier 3 accessories at Tier 2 prices, which is either a market inefficiency or a political statement depending on your perspective.
story_hooks: A Tessera Corponation internal audit has flagged an unusual volume of SDC-1 accessory components being sold through a third-party gray market that ends up on KPR-55Us — Tessera wants to know if Kang-Petrov is deliberately undercutting their accessory revenue, or if a Tessera engineer has been selling proprietary specs, and they are willing to pay for the answer.

The KPR-55U recovered from a shooting near a Zheng-dao Bioelectric distribution hub has a suppressor that forensic analysis traces to a batch manufactured by a licensed Arcturus Defense Solutions contractor — someone is supplying suppressed KP rifles to an operation that has Arcturus's fingerprints on the hardware.
